identity.title: Stemmer sign: inability to pinch a skin fold at the base of the 2nd toe

technique.how: With the patient standing (or supine), grasp the dorsal skin over the proximal phalanx of the second toe (or just proximal to the metatarsophalangeal joint; hand: index finger) between thumb and index finger and try to lift a thin skin fold. Compare with the contralateral limb.
technique.prerequisites: Foot exposed and clean; examine both feet; note BMI and any pitting.
technique.contraindications: None; avoid forceps or forceful pinching on fragile or ulcerated skin.

interpretation.positive_finding: Positive (Kaposi-Stemmer sign) when the skin cannot be pinched into a fold because of thickened, fibrotic dorsal skin, indicating lymphedema (primary or secondary) rather than venous, cardiac, hepatic or renal edema.
interpretation.negative_finding: A pinchable fold argues against established lymphedema but does not exclude early (stage 1) or lean-patient lymphedema; venous edema, DVT and systemic causes remain possible.
interpretation.pitfalls: Obesity and immobility (e.g. neuromuscular disease) give false positives, and stage 1 disease or normal BMI give false negatives; chronic venous obstruction is the commonest cause of lymphedema-like signs with normal lymphoscintigraphy. Accuracy figures come from lymphedema-referral populations, not unselected edema.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive shifts unilateral/asymmetric edema toward lymphedema (consider lymphoscintigraphy, cancer/filarial causes); negative does not exclude it - still evaluate DVT and venous disease.

estimates.target_condition: Lymphedema (primary or secondary, arm or leg)
estimates.population: 110 consecutive patients (mean age 35 y, range 1-88; 90 lower limb, 20 upper limb) referred to a tertiary Lymphedema Program, examined by a single senior surgeon
estimates.reference_standard: Lymphoscintigraphy (delayed tracer transit to inguinal/axillary nodes or dermal backflow = lymphedema)
estimates.computed_from: 2x2 from abstract: TP 80, FP 7, FN 10, TN 13. Sensitivity = 80/90 = 0.889; specificity = 13/20 = 0.65; LR+ = 0.889/0.35 = 2.54; LR- = 0.111/0.65 = 0.17; prevalence = 90/110 = 0.818. The paper labels 80/87 (0.92) 'sensitivity' and 13/23 (0.57) 'specificity', which are actually PPV and NPV.
estimates.quote: positive Stemmer sign (n = 87) exhibited abnormal (n = 80) or normal (n = 7) lymphatic function by lymphoscintigraphy (sensitivity = 92%)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; same counts in Results paragraph 1 of PMC full text (PMC6635205)

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: any classic clinical sign of lymphedema (dorsal hump, square toes, Kaposi-Stemmer sign, or nonpitting edema) - per-limb analysis
estimates.population: 436 swollen lower limbs (of 636 consecutive limbs, 12-month period) that underwent lymphoscintigraphy at a venous/lymphatic referral center; retrospective
estimates.reference_standard: Lymphoscintigraphy scored on transit delay, dermal backflow, collaterals, uptake intensity and node counts
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.17/(1-0.88) = 1.42; LR- = (1-0.17)/0.88 = 0.94, from reported composite sensitivity 17% and specificity 88%; prevalence = 258/436 = 0.59 abnormal lymphoscintigraphy
estimates.quote: Sensitivity and specificity of clinical signs in predicting lymphoscintigraphy-confirmed lymphedema were 17% and 88%, respectively.

sources.citation: Goss JA, Greene AK. Sensitivity and Specificity of the Stemmer Sign for Lymphedema: A Clinical Lymphoscintigraphic Study. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open. 2019.
Jayaraj A, Raju S, May C, Pace N. The diagnostic unreliability of classic physical signs of lymphedema. J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord. 2019.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative Stemmer sign to dismiss acute unilateral leg swelling - DVT must be excluded on its own merits; a positive sign in an obese or immobile patient is unreliable.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Rapidly progressive unilateral swelling, pain, warmth or erythema needs DVT and cellulitis/necrotizing infection assessment regardless of the Stemmer sign; new lymphedema in an adult warrants evaluation for pelvic/abdominal malignancy.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No inter-observer data; Goss 2019 used a single examiner (senior author) pinching proximal to the MTP joint rather than over the proximal phalanx as originally described (PMC full text, Discussion).

extraction_notes: Goss 2019: the abstract's 'sensitivity = 92%' is 80/87 (PPV) and 'specificity = 57%' is 13/23 (NPV); the true sensitivity and specificity from the reported 2x2 are 80/90 = 0.889 and 13/20 = 0.65 and are entered as computed. High prevalence (0.82) reflects a lymphedema referral clinic, so PPV is inflated relative to a general edema population. Jayaraj 2019 is a composite of four signs analysed per limb (only entered with COMPOSITE prefix); for the Stemmer sign alone it reports only 'the Kaposi-Stemmer sign was a significant predictor of lymphedema (odds ratio, 7.9; P = .02)' (Abstract, Results) and that 32% of sign-positive limbs had the Stemmer sign, without a sign-specific sens/spec. Kappa/inter-observer data not found. A 2025 CART study on lipedema vs lymphedema (PMID 40009424) was not reviewed (budget).
